elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement, or upon the effective date of termination of a Party's participation in this Agreement...", so the trigger covers both expiry and every form of termination, including a single Party's withdrawal under 18.1.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The insertion commits only to "a period of not less than ninety (90) days"; no six-month (or longer) assistance period appears anywhere in the operative text.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis is stated for the assistance; the words "then-current rates" (or any rate mechanic) are absent from the inserted paragraph and from 18.1-18.7.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall export and deliver to that Party, within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, all data and information belonging to, supplied by, or held or processed on behalf of that Party."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The delivery obligation specifies no format; "commonly used, machine-readable format" language was deliberately omitted.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written certification obligation appears after the export/delivery duty; Paragraph 31 confidentiality survival imposes no deletion certificate.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Trigger is "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement, or upon the effective date of termination of a Party's participation in this Agreement", so the assistance and export duties attach to every covered end-of-term event, not just anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "the other Parties shall provide that Party with reasonable transition assistance for a period of not less than ninety (90) days following such expiry or termination" - a firm floor, not a best-efforts or agree-to-agree duty like 18.4.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall export and deliver to that Party, within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, all data and information belonging to, supplied by, or held or processed on behalf of that Party" - deadline runs from the termination/expiry event, not from a request.

All four deterministic gates report ok (operation applies, data return/transition present, minimality, element coverage), and substantive inspection confirms the inserted sentence carries the 90-day and 30-day obligations rather than merely reciting the words.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the single inserted sentence supplies all three fallback elements - an expiry-or-termination trigger, a minimum ninety-day assistance period, and a thirty-day export deadline measured from the termination event.

Preferred level fails on four elements (six-month duration, then-current rates, machine-readable format, certified deletion after return); to reach preferred the drafter would need to extend the period to six months, add "at the other Parties' then-current rates", specify "in a commonly used, machine-readable format", and add a post-return deletion-and-written-certification limb.

Correctly classified as missing: nothing in 18.1-18.7 returns or exports a withdrawing Party's data (18.5 reallocates interests, 18.6 liquidates and distributes sale proceeds, 18.7 preserves accrued third-party liabilities), and 18.4 is an agreement to negotiate with no duration or deadline.

Minimal: the redline is a pure insertion with no deletion or paraphrase of existing 18.1-18.7 language, adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure, or other model-language extra, and does not duplicate any existing operative term. The mutual "the other Parties" / "that Party" formulation is necessary in this multiparty consortium structure, which has no single Vendor role, and it captures our own entitlement as a withdrawing Party.

Preserves intent: 18.5's reallocation of interests, 18.6's decommissioning and asset-realization mechanics, 18.7's accrued-liability carve-out, and the Paragraph 31 confidentiality survival all operate unchanged; the new duty adds no contradiction, undefined term, or dangling cross-reference.

Housekeeping only: the comment identifies the insertion as Subparagraph 18.8 but the rendered text carries no clause number - add the "18.8" designation so the internal numbering of Paragraph 18 stays consecutive.
